title: Design a payment system
prompt: Money cannot be lost, double-spent, or silently dropped — correctness and DURABILITY dominate raw speed. A user submits a payment that must be authorized, recorded exactly once in a strongly-consistent ledger (the source of truth), and then settled asynchronously with downstream banks/processors. Draw how a payment flows from the client, through an API gateway and a payment service, into a durable ledger, and how settlement, event fan-out, and idempotent retries happen off the critical path via a queue. Show that a transient failure or duplicate submission never corrupts the balance.

criteria.label: Payment request originates from a client
criteria.metWhy: Good — the flow starts from the paying user/client.
criteria.why: Add a User/Client node to show where the payment request originates.

criteria.label: Requests enter through an API gateway / entry tier
criteria.metWhy: Good — a gateway/edge fronts the system for auth, routing, and rate limiting.
criteria.why: Front the system with an API Gateway (or Load Balancer) so requests are authenticated and routed before hitting the payment service.

criteria.label: A payment service handles authorization and orchestration
criteria.metWhy: Good — a dedicated payment service owns authorization and write orchestration.
criteria.why: Add a Server/Service to process payments — validating, authorizing, and orchestrating the ledger write and settlement.

criteria.label: Strongly-consistent ledger as the source of truth
criteria.metWhy: Good — a durable, strongly-consistent ledger is the single source of truth for balances.
criteria.why: Add a Database to serve as the transactional ledger. Money requires a durable, strongly-consistent store — not a cache or in-memory state.

criteria.label: Payment service writes to the ledger
criteria.metWhy: Good — the service commits each payment to the ledger on the write path.
criteria.why: Connect the payment Service to the Database so authorized payments are durably committed to the ledger.

criteria.label: Queue for async settlement, event fan-out, and idempotent retries
criteria.metWhy: Good — a queue moves settlement and events off the critical path with safe, idempotent retries.
criteria.why: Add a Queue so settlement with downstream processors and event fan-out happen asynchronously, and failed payments can be retried idempotently without corrupting balances.

criteria.label: Payment service publishes to the settlement queue
criteria.metWhy: Good — the service emits settlement/events to the queue after recording the payment.
criteria.why: Connect the payment Service to the Queue so settlement work and events are enqueued after the ledger write.

criteria.label: Monitoring/alerting on payments and reconciliation
criteria.metWhy: Good — monitoring catches stuck payments, failed settlements, and reconciliation drift.
criteria.why: Add a Monitoring node to track payment success/failure rates, settlement lag, and reconciliation alerts — critical when money is on the line.
